## TL;DR

A small, well-structured extension — 298 lines of TypeScript across three files with a clean
extension-host/webview split and a layered XSS defense that holds up under testing. The one thing
to fix first is a `URIError` in the image-path rewriter that silently and permanently kills the
view for any file containing a raw HTML `<img>` with a bare `%` in its path — reproduced end to
end, and reachable precisely because `html: true` is enabled for CLIO's HTML comments. Security
posture, file-watching strategy, and packaging hygiene are already correct.

| # | Do this | Why it's first | Where |
|---|---------|----------------|-------|
| 1 | ~~Guard `decodeURIComponent` and wrap `update()` in try/catch~~ ✅ done `7ebe5ea` | A plausible input silently bricked the view with no error shown | `src/render.ts` (`decodePath`) |
| 2 | ~~Make `package` script run `build` first~~ ✅ done `615c572` | The release command silently shipped a stale bundle | `package.json` scripts |
| 3 | ~~Decide what to do with `docs/0. Claude Prompts.md`~~ ✅ done — history rewritten, file gitignored | Was 8,834 lines of third-party paths and client names | `docs/` (now ignored) |

## What this repo does well

- **The XSS defense is genuinely layered, and it holds.** Ten injection vectors were run through
  verbatim copies of `sanitize()` and the CSP. Every script-execution path is blocked twice —
  once by the regex pass (`src/render.ts:21-26`) and once by `default-src 'none'` plus a nonce'd
  `script-src` (`src/markdownViewProvider.ts:174-180`). `<script>`, `onerror=`, `onload=`, and
  `javascript:` hrefs were all neutralized; `<iframe>` survives the regex but is stopped dead by
  CSP. Belt-and-braces was the stated intent in the comment, and it is what was built.

- **The file watcher is bound to the parent directory, not the file.** `src/markdownViewProvider.ts:209-219`
  watches `path.dirname(file)` with the reasoning recorded in a comment: atomic-rename saves break
  an inode-bound watch. Testing confirms this survives deleting and recreating the whole directory
  on macOS — the watcher keeps firing. This is the non-obvious correct choice.

- **The webview never receives raw file content.** `update()` posts fully-prepared state messages
  (`src/markdownViewProvider.ts:137-144`) and `media/main.js` only renders them. The placeholder
  and error UI is built with `createElement`/`textContent` (`media/main.js:29-54`), so error
  strings containing a file path can't inject markup — the one place untrusted-ish text meets the
  DOM is handled correctly.

- **Config scope is coherent end to end.** `scope: "application"` in the manifest is matched by
  `vscode.ConfigurationTarget.Global` at the write site (`src/markdownViewProvider.ts:86`), with a
  comment explaining the pairing. The "one file, every window" claim in the README is actually
  enforced by both halves.

- **Packaging hygiene is already right.** `.vscodeignore` excludes `src/`, `docs/`, `node_modules/`,
  and `dist/*.map`; the produced `.vsix` is 8 files / 73 KB. The `F5` workflow documented in the
  README is backed by a real `.vscode/launch.json` with a `preLaunchTask` that builds first.

- **Scroll position survives refresh and view toggling**, keyed by file + mode and persisted
  through `getState`/`setState` (`media/main.js:56-77`) — the VS Code-idiomatic mechanism rather
  than an ad-hoc cache.

## Findings — top 7 by leverage

### F1: `decodeURIComponent` throws on raw HTML image paths, silently killing the view [HIGH] — ✅ FIXED 2026-07-28 (`7ebe5ea`)

**Where:** `src/markdownViewProvider.ts:153` · commit `0fb8d13`

> **Resolution (7ebe5ea):** decodePath() falls back to the literal path on a malformed escape, and the render step is wrapped so any failure posts the error state instead of rejecting. Covered by a regression test that fails when the fix is reverted.

`rewriteImageSources()` calls `decodeURIComponent(src)` on every non-absolute `<img src="…">` in
the rendered HTML. markdown-it's own `![](…)` syntax is safe — it percent-encodes stray `%`
characters, so `![a](100%.png)` becomes `src="100%25.png"` and decodes cleanly. Raw HTML does not
go through that normalizer: `html: true` (`src/render.ts:4`) passes `<img src="90%.png">` through
verbatim, and `decodeURIComponent("90%.png")` throws `URIError: URI malformed`.

The throw escapes the `String.replace` callback, out of `update()`. Every caller invokes it as
`void this.update()` (lines 56, 66, 227), so the rejection is unhandled: no error state is posted,
no message is logged to the user, and the view keeps displaying whatever it last rendered. Every
subsequent update on that file throws at the same point, so the view stays frozen until the file
changes or the window reloads.

Reproduced end to end through verbatim copies of `sanitize()` and `rewriteImageSources()`:

```
input markdown contains a raw HTML <img> (allowed: html:true)
*** update() THREW: URIError: URI malformed
```

**Impact:** One `<img src="…%…">` anywhere in the configured file permanently freezes the sidebar
with no visible error. Because `html: true` was enabled specifically so CLIO's raw HTML passes
through, raw `<img>` tags are an expected input class, not a hypothetical one.

**Fix:** Two independent changes, both worth making.

1. Make the decode non-throwing — in `rewriteImageSources`, replace line 153:

```ts
// was: const decoded = decodeURIComponent(src);
let decoded: string;
try {
  decoded = decodeURIComponent(src);
} catch {
  decoded = src; // malformed percent-escape: treat the path as literal
}
```

2. Stop any future render error from silently freezing the view — wrap the render step in
`update()` (around lines 131-135) so failures surface in the existing error state:

```ts
let html: string;
try {
  html = this.mode === 'rendered'
    ? this.rewriteImageSources(renderMarkdown(text), path.dirname(file), view.webview)
    : `<pre class="source">${escapeHtml(text)}</pre>`;
} catch (error) {
  void view.webview.postMessage({
    type: 'state', state: 'error',
    message: `${file} — render failed: ${error instanceof Error ? error.message : String(error)}`,
    styleClass: this.styleClass,
  });
  return;
}
```

### F2: `npm run package` does not build, so it can ship a stale bundle [MEDIUM] — ✅ FIXED 2026-07-28 (`615c572`)

**Where:** `package.json:139` · commit `07b5ab3` (README claim at `README.md:35` · commit `0344492`)

> **Resolution (615c572):** package now runs `npm run build:prod && vsce package` (build:prod added later in 44af94a).

The script is `"package": "vsce package"`. It bundles whatever `dist/extension.js` happens to be
on disk. `README.md:35` documents it as "build the installable `.vsix`", which reads as though it
compiles. `dist/` is gitignored, so on a fresh clone the first `npm run package` fails outright;
on an existing checkout it silently packages the previous build.

**Impact:** Source edits followed by `npm run package` produce a `.vsix` containing the *old* code,
with no warning. The artifact installs and runs normally, so the discrepancy shows up as "my change
didn't do anything" rather than as an error. Nothing in the repo catches this.

**Fix:** Chain the build, matching how `build` already chains `check`:

```json
"package": "npm run build && vsce package"
```

Optionally add `--allow-missing-repository` to silence the one warning `vsce` emits for a private
extension, or add a `repository` field to the manifest.

### F3: An 8,834-line third-party prompt transcript is committed [MEDIUM] — ✅ RESOLVED 2026-07-28

**Where:** `docs/0. Claude Prompts.md` · was added in the root commit `2f52218` (now pruned)

> **Resolution:** history was rewritten with `git filter-branch --index-filter` across all 6
> commits, dropping the path everywhere. `refs/original/` was deleted, the reflog expired, and
> `git gc --prune=now` run, so the blob is unreachable — not merely untracked. The root commit
> contained only this file, so `--prune-empty` removed it; history is now 5 commits and every SHA
> changed (`2ad949e→0344492`, `e921e70→15f73db`, `7654afd→f322615`, `f5e010b→0fb8d13`,
> `5ef0a74→07b5ab3`). The file remains on disk as the test fixture, byte-identical
> (sha256 `aa49593c…`), and `docs/` is now in `.gitignore:8`. Verified: no commit or tree
> references the path, and no reachable object carries it.
>
> The original description follows for the record.

The file is a CLIO prompt log used as sample content. Scanning it: **no live credential values**
(the `sk-…` hits are slugs such as `sk-self-remove-dead-qwen-path`, not keys). It does contain 177
references to `/Users/noelsaw/` — another person's home directory — including paths to their
secrets directory (`/Users/noelsaw/secrets/xyz/qwen.txt`, `/Users/noelsaw/secrets/ltvera/…`),
private org and repo names (`NeochromeTeam/sleuth-app`), and client names.

`git remote -v` returns empty — this repo has no remote, so nothing has been published. It is
correctly excluded from the `.vsix` by `.vscodeignore`, so it does not ship to users either.

**Impact:** None today. It becomes a disclosure the moment a remote is added and pushed, and it is
in git history, so deleting the file later does not remove it from the repo. The window to fix it
cheaply is before the first push.

**Fix:** Decide which of these applies, and act before adding a remote:

- **Keep it local only:** add `docs/` to `.gitignore` and `git rm --cached "docs/0. Claude Prompts.md"`.
  History still contains it — acceptable if the repo stays local or private forever.
- **Intend to publish:** rewrite history to drop the file
  (`git filter-repo --path "docs/0. Claude Prompts.md" --invert-paths`), or, given the repo is only
  6 commits old with no remote, squash to a fresh initial commit without it.
- **Need sample content:** replace it with a short synthetic fixture (20-30 lines exercising
  headings, code blocks, tables, HTML comments, and a raw `<img>` — which would also cover F1).

### F4: CSP nonce is generated with `Math.random()` [LOW] — ✅ FIXED 2026-07-28 (`7435acc`)

**Where:** `src/markdownViewProvider.ts:238-245` · commit `0fb8d13`

> **Resolution (7435acc):** createNonce() uses randomBytes(24) from node:crypto.

`createNonce()` builds a 32-character nonce from `Math.floor(Math.random() * …)`. `Math.random()`
is not cryptographically secure and its internal state is recoverable from observed output, so the
nonce is predictable in principle rather than unguessable.

**Impact:** Low in practice — a predicted nonce only matters to an attacker who can also inject an
inline `<script>` into the rendered HTML, and `sanitize()` strips `<script>` blocks before CSP is
ever consulted (verified against 10 vectors). This is a weakened layer in a defense that currently
holds elsewhere, not an open hole. It is a one-line fix, which is why it is worth doing.

**Fix:** Use the crypto module already available in the extension host:

```ts
import { randomBytes } from 'node:crypto';

function createNonce(): string {
  return randomBytes(24).toString('base64');
}
```

Base64 output is valid in a CSP nonce and the `possible`/loop scaffolding can be deleted.

### F5: CSP permits loading images from any HTTPS host [LOW]

**MRT:** Known trade-off. Not fixing this as it might interfere with possible use-case of wanting to load remote images.

**Where:** `src/markdownViewProvider.ts:177` · commit `0fb8d13`

The policy is `img-src ${webview.cspSource} https: data:`. Testing confirms
`<img src="https://evil.test/pixel.png">` survives `sanitize()` and is permitted by CSP, so it
loads when the file renders.

**Impact:** Any remote image in the configured markdown file — including a 1×1 tracking pixel
pasted in from elsewhere — fires a request on render, disclosing IP address, approximate time of
reading, and how often the file is viewed. For a personal notes viewer this is a privacy leak
rather than a compromise; nothing is executed and no local data is sent.

**Fix:** If remote images are not needed (likely for a local prompt log), drop `https:` so only
local files resolved through `asWebviewUri` load:

```ts
`img-src ${webview.cspSource} data:`,
```

If remote images are wanted, this is a deliberate trade-off — record it in the comment above the
CSP array so it does not read as an oversight later.

### F6: `retainContextWhenHidden` duplicates state persistence that is already implemented [LOW] — ✅ FIXED 2026-07-28 (`3bcb7a9`)

**Where:** `src/extension.ts:9` · commit `07b5ab3`

> **Resolution (3bcb7a9):** retainContextWhenHidden removed; the getState/setState scroll persistence already covered it. A comment records the choice.

The provider is registered with `webviewOptions: { retainContextWhenHidden: true }`, which keeps
the hidden webview's full DOM and JS context resident. VS Code's own guidance is to prefer
`getState`/`setState` for exactly this reason — and `media/main.js:56-77` already implements that,
persisting scroll position keyed by file and mode.

**Impact:** The extension holds a live webview context for the entire session even when the view is
never opened again, for a benefit the `setState` path already delivers. On a large rendered log this
is real memory the editor cannot reclaim.

**Fix:** Remove the option and confirm the restore path covers the gap:

```ts
vscode.window.registerWebviewViewProvider(MarkdownViewProvider.viewId, provider),
```

The trade-off is a brief re-render when the view is reshown. If that flash is unacceptable, keep the
flag and add a comment saying the memory cost is accepted deliberately — the current code reads as
though the two mechanisms are unaware of each other.

### F7: Concurrent `update()` calls have no sequencing guard [LOW] — ✅ FIXED 2026-07-28 (`d2dac67`)

**Where:** `src/markdownViewProvider.ts:106-145` · commit `0fb8d13`

> **Resolution (d2dac67):** update() stamps each run with a monotonic sequence number and drops superseded results before they reach the webview.

`update()` is entered from three paths — `refresh()` (line 56), `setMode()` (line 66), and the
debounced watcher callback (line 227) — and performs an `await fs.promises.readFile` before posting
its result. Nothing prevents two invocations from overlapping, and nothing marks which result is
newer.

**Impact:** If an earlier read completes after a later one (plausible on a network share, an
external drive, or a large file), the webview is left showing the older content, and no further
event arrives to correct it until the next file change. Low probability on a local SSD.

**Fix:** Add a monotonic token and discard stale results:

```ts
private updateSeq = 0;

private async update(): Promise<void> {
  const seq = ++this.updateSeq;
  // … after each await, before every postMessage:
  if (seq !== this.updateSeq) { return; }
  // … existing postMessage
}
```

Apply the check immediately before each of the three `postMessage` calls (lines 114, 122, 137).

## Appendix — remaining findings (11)

- **A1** ✅ FIXED `94abd22` [MEDIUM] `package.json:150` — `typescript` is pinned to `^5.6.0` while TypeScript 7.0.2 is
  current; TS 7 is the native-port rewrite and a deliberate deferral, but nothing records that
  decision. — Fix: add a comment or `.nvmrc`-style note stating 5.x is intentional.
- **A2** ✅ FIXED `9368180` [LOW] `src/markdownViewProvider.ts:215-219` — `fs.watch` returns an EventEmitter with no
  `.on('error')` listener; an unhandled `'error'` event throws. Could not be triggered on macOS
  (directory deletion and recreation both stayed silent, and the watcher survived), so this is
  latent rather than demonstrated. — Fix: `this.watcher.on('error', () => this.disposeWatcher())`.
- **A3** ✅ FIXED `f4928df` [LOW] `src/markdownViewProvider.ts:149` — the image-rewrite regex only matches
  double-quoted `src="…"`; raw HTML using `src='…'` is left unrewritten and the image silently
  fails to load. — Fix: extend the pattern to accept single quotes, or parse rather than regex.
- **A4** [LOW] `src/markdownViewProvider.ts:163-166` — `localResourceRoots` contains only the
  markdown file's own directory, so `![](../assets/x.png)` is blocked with no message. — Fix: add
  the parent directory, or surface a hint when an image URI resolves outside the roots.
- **A5** ✅ FIXED `77de550` [LOW] `src/markdownViewProvider.ts:75` — `openInEditor()` calls `showTextDocument` without
  checking the file exists; a stale configured path produces a raw VS Code error rather than the
  friendly message used at line 72. — Fix: `fs.promises.access` first, reuse the existing message.
- **A6** [LOW] `src/markdownViewProvider.ts:120` — the whole file is read into memory and rendered
  in full on every change, with no size ceiling; `README.md:40` already flags this as a roadmap
  item for very large logs. — Fix: short-circuit above a threshold with a "file too large" state.
- **A7** ✅ FIXED `44af94a` [LOW] `package.json:136` — the esbuild invocation has no `--minify` and no dev/prod split,
  so the shipped bundle is 247 KB unminified. — Fix: add `--minify` to a production-only script.
- **A8** ✅ FIXED `5df74d8` [PROCESS] No CI — `.github/` does not exist; nothing verifies that `main` compiles. — Fix:
  a workflow running `npm ci && npm run build`.
- **A9** ✅ FIXED `f284345` [PROCESS] No tests — 0 test files tracked, and no `test` script. `src/render.ts` is pure
  and trivially testable. — Fix: see upgrade path step 4.
- **A10** ✅ FIXED `5a44a90` [PROCESS] No linter — no ESLint or Prettier config, so style and common-error rules are
  unenforced across the four source files. — Fix: `@typescript-eslint` with the recommended set.
- **A11** [PROCESS] No git remote and no `LICENSE` file (manifest declares `UNLICENSED`, and `vsce`
  warns on both `repository` and `LICENSE`). — Fix: intentional for a private extension; add both
  if it is ever published.

## Not checked

- **Branch protection and PR review history** — the repo has no configured remote (`git remote -v`
  is empty), so there is no upstream to inspect. `gh` is authenticated and available; this check
  becomes applicable once a remote exists.
- **Runtime behavior in a live Extension Development Host** — findings were verified by static
  reading plus standalone Node reproductions of the exact code paths (`sanitize`,
  `rewriteImageSources`, `fs.watch`). F1 was reproduced this way rather than by driving the VS Code
  UI.
- **Cross-platform watcher behavior** — `fs.watch` was exercised on macOS only. Linux (inotify) and
  Windows differ in how directory deletion and recreation are reported; A2 may present differently
  there.
- **`media/view.css` and `media/icon.svg`** — reviewed for correctness but assessed as presentation
  only; no findings raised, and visual fidelity to the CLIO app was not evaluated.
- **AI-tooling lens** — not applicable. `git ls-files | grep -iE 'AGENTS|CLAUDE|cursorrules|SKILL'`
  matches nothing; `docs/0. Claude Prompts.md` is sample content, not instructions to an agent.
